title: Factorial Number
problem_statement: Read a non-negative integer n and print its factorial, written n!. The factorial is the product of all positive integers from 1 through n. By definition, 0! is 1.
input_format: One line containing one integer n in the inclusive range 0 through 20.
output_format: Print one integer equal to n!, with no labels or extra text.

if __name__ == "__main__":

public_samples.explanation: 20 is the maximum allowed input; its factorial is 2432902008176640000.

hints: A factorial is a product, not a sum. Consider what value should leave a product unchanged.
Start from the identity value for multiplication, then multiply by the positive integers up to n.
Initialize the result to 1 and loop over the inclusive range from 1 through n. If n is 0, the loop runs zero times and the result remains 1.
common_beginner_mistakes: Starting the accumulator at 0, which makes every product remain 0.
Returning 0 for n = 0 instead of applying the definition 0! = 1.
Adding the loop values instead of multiplying them.
Stopping the loop before n and omitting the final factor.
Starting the loop at 0 and multiplying by zero.
Using a fixed-width assumption that cannot hold the maximum result; Python integers can represent the result for the stated constraints.
completion_criteria: Computes the product of every positive integer from 1 through n.
Prints the exact integer result without labels or extra text.
Passes all public samples and separately maintained private tests.
